title: Instructions for Godly Living
overview: 1 Timothy 6 provides practical instructions for Christian conduct, emphasizing godliness, contentment, and the dangers of loving money. Paul addresses servants, urging respect for masters to uphold God's name, and warns against false teachers who distort sound doctrine. The chapter contrasts the pursuit of wealth with spiritual gain, encouraging believers to flee greed and pursue righteousness, faith, love, patience, and meekness. It concludes with a solemn charge to Timothy to guard the gospel against false teachings and to exhort the rich to be generous and humble. This chapter serves as a vital guide for maintaining integrity, faithfulness, and godliness in the midst of worldly temptations and challenges.
structure:
**Verses 1-2: Instructions to Servants.** Paul exhorts servants to honor their masters, especially emphasizing respect even when masters are believers, to prevent blasphemy against God’s name.

**Verses 3-5: Warning Against False Teachers.** Paul condemns those who teach contrary to sound doctrine, describing their pride, ignorance, and corrupt motives, particularly their erroneous belief that gain is godliness.

**Verses 6-10: The Value of Godliness and the Danger of Riches.** The chapter contrasts godliness with contentment as true gain, warns of the temptations and destruction that come from the love of money, and identifies it as the root of all evil.

**Verses 11-16: Exhortation to Timothy.** Paul charges Timothy to pursue virtues such as righteousness and faith, to fight the good fight, and to keep the commandment until Christ’s appearing, highlighting Christ’s sovereign authority.

**Verses 17-19: Instructions to the Rich.** The wealthy are urged not to be arrogant or trust in riches but to be rich in good works, generous, and ready to share, storing up a foundation for eternal life.

**Verses 20-21: Final Charge to Timothy.** Timothy is admonished to guard the entrusted gospel, avoiding profane and vain babblings and false knowledge that lead to faith errors.

keyVerses.text: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
keyVerses.significance: This verse encapsulates the chapter’s central teaching that true wealth is found in a godly life combined with contentment, contrasting worldly pursuits of riches.

keyVerses.text: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
keyVerses.significance: This verse warns of the spiritual dangers of coveting money, highlighting how it leads to faith’s downfall and personal sorrow, a key theme in the chapter.

keyVerses.text: Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.
keyVerses.significance: Paul’s exhortation to Timothy to actively pursue faith and eternal life underscores the chapter’s call to perseverance and steadfastness in Christian living.

keyVerses.text: O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called:
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights the importance of guarding the gospel against false teachings and empty arguments, a critical concern for the early church and today.

characters.name: Paul
characters.description: The apostle writing to Timothy, providing pastoral guidance on godly living, warning against false teachers, and encouraging faithfulness in ministry.

characters.name: Timothy
characters.description: Paul’s young protégé and pastor, charged to guard the gospel, avoid false teachings, and lead the church with integrity and godliness.

characters.name: False Teachers
characters.description: Individuals who promote erroneous doctrines, particularly equating gain with godliness, causing division and spiritual harm within the church.

characters.name: God
characters.description: The sovereign Creator and Judge, described as immortal and dwelling in unapproachable light, who commands holiness and rewards faithfulness.

themes.description: The chapter emphasizes that true gain comes not from wealth but from living a godly life with contentment, reflecting a heart fixed on eternal values.
A key warning against covetousness and the love of money, which leads to spiritual ruin, false teaching, and personal sorrow, contrasting with godly trust.
Timothy is urged to guard the gospel and fight the good fight of faith, highlighting the necessity of perseverance and vigilance in ministry.
Instructions to servants to honor their masters demonstrate the importance of maintaining godly order and witness in social relationships.

historicalContext: Written around the mid-first century AD, this letter addresses the church in Ephesus, a major city in Asia Minor known for its pagan worship and social stratification. Slavery was a common institution, and the early Christian community included both slaves and masters, necessitating guidance on conduct within these relationships. False teachers were active, promoting heresies that threatened the church’s unity and sound doctrine. The Roman Empire’s political environment was stable but often hostile to Christian distinctiveness, making Paul’s pastoral instructions crucial for maintaining faithfulness under pressure.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Emphasizes the sovereignty of God and the call to godliness as evidence of true faith. The warning against the love of money is seen as a call to trust God’s provision and reject worldly temptations.

Highlights the pastoral nature of the epistle, focusing on the church age’s distinct challenges, including false teaching and social order, interpreting the call to godliness as part of the believer’s sanctification.
Early commentators like Augustine saw this chapter as a call to humility and charity, warning against greed and urging believers to pursue virtues that reflect Christ’s character.

crossReferences.connection: Echoes the instruction for servants to respect their masters, emphasizing obedience to church leaders for God’s sake.
Jesus’ teaching that one cannot serve both God and money parallels the warning against the love of money in 1 Timothy 6.
The call to pure religion and caring for those in need complements the exhortation for the rich to do good works and be generous.
Paul’s metaphor of fighting the good fight of faith is reiterated, underscoring perseverance in the Christian life.
Warns against the pursuit of riches, aligning with the chapter’s teaching on the fleeting nature of wealth.

application: Respect and honor those in authority as a testimony to God’s name.
Guard your heart against the love of money by cultivating contentment and trust in God’s provision.
Pursue godliness actively through faith, love, patience, and humility.
Be vigilant against false teachings by grounding yourself in sound doctrine.
Use wealth generously to do good works and support others in need.
Persevere in your faith, remembering the eternal reward promised by Christ.
conclusion: 1 Timothy 6 remains a timeless exhortation to live a life marked by godliness, contentment, and faithful stewardship. It warns believers of the spiritual dangers posed by greed and false teaching while encouraging perseverance in the faith and generosity toward others. By following Paul’s instructions, Christians today can maintain integrity in their relationships, guard the truth of the gospel, and focus on eternal riches rather than temporal wealth, thereby honoring God in all aspects of life.
timeline: c. AD 63-65 - Paul's Pastoral Epistles during his imprisonment in Rome

definitions.definition: A lifestyle characterized by reverence for God, moral integrity, and devotion to His commands.
A state of satisfaction and peace with one’s circumstances, trusting in God’s provision.
Irreverent or disrespectful toward what is sacred, often referring to speech or behavior.

definitions.term: Oppositions of science falsely so called
definitions.definition: False knowledge or teachings that appear scholarly but contradict the gospel truth.
A ruler with great power; here referring to Christ as the supreme King.

outline.heading: Instructions to Servants and Masters
outline.description: Paul instructs servants to honor their masters to uphold God’s name, emphasizing respect even when masters are fellow believers.

outline.heading: Warning Against False Teachers
outline.description: Paul condemns those who teach contrary to sound doctrine, highlighting their pride and corrupt motives, and advises withdrawal from them.

outline.heading: The Value of Godliness Over Wealth
outline.description: The chapter contrasts godliness with contentment as true gain and warns about the spiritual dangers of loving money.

outline.heading: Exhortation to Timothy to Pursue Virtue
outline.description: Paul urges Timothy to flee evil, pursue righteousness and faith, and keep the commandment until Christ’s return.

outline.heading: Instructions to the Rich
outline.description: The wealthy are encouraged to be humble, generous, and rich in good works, storing up eternal rewards.

outline.heading: Final Charge to Timothy
outline.description: Timothy is charged to guard the gospel against false teachings and empty arguments that lead to faith errors.
